accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding food entitlements under the Andhra Pradesh PDS:
1. A Priority Household receives 5 kg of rice per unit free of cost.
2. An Antyodaya Anna Yojana household receives 35 kg of rice per card free of cost.
3. Wheat is supplied at 1 kg per card at Rs 16 per kg.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. PHH entitlement is 5 kg per unit, AAY entitlement is 35 kg per card, and wheat is supplied at 1 kg per card at Rs 16 per kg.
accepted.tq: Check each entitlement separately before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: AP ration distribution - doorstep vehicles (MDU), rice card

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the millet entitlement under the Andhra Pradesh PDS?
o: 35 kg of ragi per card for AAY households only
Up to 3 kg per card of ragi for all areas and jowar in Rayalaseema, free of cost, in lieu of rice
5 kg of jowar per unit for PHH households at the market price
3 kg per unit of wheat throughout Andhra Pradesh at Rs 16 per kg
accepted.x: Ragi for all areas and jowar in Rayalaseema may be supplied up to 3 kg per card free of cost in lieu of rice.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between commodity, region, quantity and mode of substitution.
accepted.sec: AP ration distribution - doorstep vehicles (MDU), rice card

accepted.s: Which of the following is associated with the AP e-PDS system?

Cash-only transactions without portability
100% Aadhaar seeding, biometric transactions and intra-state portability
Inter-state portability without biometric authentication

accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete combination of system features.
accepted.sec: AP ration distribution - doorstep vehicles (MDU), rice card

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Law or body)
 a. National Food Security Act, 2013
 b. Essential Commodities Act, 1955
 c. Food Corporations Act, 1964
 d. Article 47

List-II (Purpose)
 i. Duty to raise nutrition and the standard of living
 ii. Creation of the Food Corporation of India
 iii. Legal right to subsidised grain and food security with dignity
 iv. Control of production, supply, price and stocks of essential goods

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i
a–iv, b–iii, c–i, d–ii
a–ii, b–i, c–iv, d–iii
a–i, b–ii, c–iii, d–iv
accepted.x: NFSA provides the legal right to subsidised grain; the Essential Commodities Act regulates essential goods; the Food Corporations Act created FCI; and Article 47 concerns nutrition and living standards.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure institutional pair and eliminate codes containing mismatches.
accepted.sec: Food and nutrition security laws and bodies - matching purpose  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Essential Commodities Act, 1955 primarily provides the basis for:
o: Creation of district grievance officers
Appointment of State Food Commissions
Constitutional recognition of the right to education
Control of production, supply, price and stocks of essential goods
accepted.x: The Essential Commodities Act enables control over the production, supply, prices and stocks of essential goods and supports PDS control orders.
accepted.tq: Match the law with its operational regulatory function.
accepted.sec: Food and nutrition security laws and bodies - matching purpose  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Food Corporations Act, 1964 is associated with the creation of:
o: FCI
Kendriya Bhandar
NAFED
NCCF
accepted.x: The Food Corporations Act, 1964 created the Food Corporation of India for procurement, storage and distribution.
accepted.tq: Use the institution-founder or institution-enabling-law association.
accepted.sec: Food and nutrition security laws and bodies - matching purpose  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Article 47 of the Constitution, in the context of food and nutrition, directs the State to:
o: Raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living
Create a separate food commission in every district
Regulate stock exchanges and securities markets
Guarantee employment in every household
accepted.x: Article 47, a Directive Principle of State Policy, concerns raising the level of nutrition and the standard of living.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the constitutional directive from statutory and administrative mechanisms.
accepted.sec: Food and nutrition security laws and bodies - matching purpose  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The TPDS (Control) Order, 2015 primarily lays down operational rules relating to:
o: Urban housing subsidies
Procurement of securities by stock exchanges
Ration cards and Fair Price Shops under NFSA
Appointment of members of the Finance Commission
accepted.x: The TPDS (Control) Order, 2015 provides operational rules for ration cards and Fair Price Shops under the NFSA framework.
accepted.tq: Identify the administrative instrument by the field it operationalises.
accepted.sec: Food and nutrition security laws and bodies - matching purpose  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which authority is designated as the grievance redressal officer at the district level under the NFSA grievance machinery?
o: District Supply Commissioner only
State Food Commission Secretary
District Grievance Redressal Officer
Food Corporation of India Chairman
accepted.x: A District Grievance Redressal Officer, or DGRO, is provided in each district for grievance redressal under the NFSA framework.
accepted.tq: Ask who performs the specific administrative function at the district level.
accepted.sec: NFSA grievance machinery - State Food Commission, DGRO, vigilance committees  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NFSA grievance machinery:
1. A State Food Commission is provided in each State.
2. An existing commission may be designated as the State Food Commission.
3. Public servants failing to comply with relief recommended by the DGRO may be penalised.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Each State has a State Food Commission, an existing body may be designated to avoid new costs, and non-compliance with DGRO recommendations can attract penalties.
accepted.tq: Test the composition, cost-saving provision and enforcement consequence together.
accepted.sec: NFSA grievance machinery - State Food Commission, DGRO, vigilance committees  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: At which levels are vigilance committees under the NFSA framework constituted?
o: State, district, block and Fair Price Shop levels
Only at the State and district levels
Only at the block and village levels
Only at the Central and State levels
accepted.x: NFSA vigilance committees function at the State, district, block and Fair Price Shop levels.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete multi-level institutional arrangement.
accepted.sec: NFSA grievance machinery - State Food Commission, DGRO, vigilance committees  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following measures strengthens transparency and social accountability in the Public Distribution System under the NFSA framework?
1. Social audits
2. Mandatory disclosure of PDS records
3. Vigilance committees
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Social audits, mandatory disclosure of PDS records and vigilance committees are all accountability mechanisms under the NFSA framework.
accepted.tq: Recognise the combination of transparency and community-monitoring mechanisms.

accepted.s: Buffer stocks in India were formally introduced during the:
o: Second Five-Year Plan
Third Five-Year Plan
Fourth Five-Year Plan
Fifth Five-Year Plan
accepted.x: Buffer stocks were formally introduced during the Fourth Five-Year Plan, covering 1969–74.
accepted.tq: Link the policy innovation with its Five-Year Plan period.
accepted.sec: Buffer stock norms - quarterly norms, strategic reserve, OMSS  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which body fixes the minimum buffer stock levels for each quarter?
o: National Food Commission
Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs
NITI Aayog
Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
accepted.x: The minimum buffer stock levels are fixed by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs and specified for each quarter.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the authority.
accepted.sec: Buffer stock norms - quarterly norms, strategic reserve, OMSS  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly lists the dates used for fixing quarterly minimum buffer stock norms?
o: 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October
1 February, 1 May, 1 August and 1 November
15 January, 15 April, 15 July and 15 October
31 March, 30 June, 30 September and 31 December
accepted.x: Quarterly buffer stock norms are fixed for 1 April, 1 July, 1 October and 1 January; the same dates are correctly listed in chronological cycle form in option a.
accepted.tq: Arrange recurring quarterly reference dates without confusing them with financial-year closing dates.
accepted.sec: Buffer stock norms - quarterly norms, strategic reserve, OMSS  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The strategic reserve component of buffer stocks consists of:
o: Only pulses held for export emergencies
Wheat and rice held for emergencies
Only imported cereals held by private traders
Sugar and edible oil held for urban consumers
accepted.x: The strategic reserve comprises wheat and rice maintained for emergency requirements.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the commodities and purpose of the strategic reserve.
accepted.sec: Buffer stock norms - quarterly norms, strategic reserve, OMSS  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: According to the cited 2026 estimate, India’s foodgrain stocks were approximately:
o: 702 lakh metric tonnes, about four times the buffer norms
502 lakh metric tonnes, about three times the buffer norms
402 lakh metric tonnes, about twice the buffer norms
602 lakh metric tonnes, about three times the buffer norms
accepted.x: The estimate placed stocks at about 602 lakh metric tonnes, roughly three times the prescribed buffer norms.
accepted.tq: Separate the current approximate stock estimate from the earlier dated stock figure.
accepted.sec: Buffer stock norms - quarterly norms, strategic reserve, OMSS  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: On 1 September 2025, the reported stock of rice and wheat was approximately:
o: Rice 369.06 lakh tonnes and wheat 332.97 lakh tonnes
Rice 332.97 lakh tonnes and wheat 369.06 lakh tonnes
Rice 369.06 lakh tonnes and wheat 302.97 lakh tonnes
Rice 339.06 lakh tonnes and wheat 332.97 lakh tonnes
accepted.x: The reported total was 702.03 lakh tonnes, comprising 369.06 lakh tonnes of rice and 332.97 lakh tonnes of wheat.
accepted.tq: Check both components and their order rather than relying only on the total.
accepted.sec: Buffer stock norms - quarterly norms, strategic reserve, OMSS  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective or effect of the Open Market Sale Scheme?
o: Replacing the Food Corporation of India’s procurement function with private procurement
Offloading excess central-pool stocks and reducing carrying costs
Moderating prices
Raising grain supply during lean seasons and in deficit regions
accepted.x: OMSS involves FCI selling surplus central-pool grain at predetermined prices. It raises supply, moderates prices, offloads excess stocks and reduces carrying costs, but it does not replace FCI procurement with private procurement.
accepted.tq: Find the option that introduces a function not belonging to the scheme.
accepted.sec: Buffer stock norms - quarterly norms, strategic reserve, OMSS  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The proportion of households unable to afford the ICMR-NIN recommended diet declined from approximately 52% in 2011–12 to approximately what proportion in 2023–24?
accepted.x: The proportion declined from about 52% to about 25% by 2023–24. The corresponding figures were about 25% in rural areas and 21% in urban areas.
accepted.tq: Recall the direction and magnitude of change using the two benchmark years.
accepted.sec: Global Hunger Index and SOFI - India's rank, indicators  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly represents the rural–urban figures for households unable to afford the ICMR-NIN recommended diet in 2023–24?
o: 25% rural and 21% urban
21% rural and 21% urban
25% rural and 25% urban
21% rural and 25% urban
accepted.x: The reported proportions were approximately 25% for rural households and 21% for urban households.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the rural and urban columns in a comparison-based figure.
accepted.sec: Global Hunger Index and SOFI - India's rank, indicators  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Bharat-brand atta, rice and dal are sold through which combination of channels as a consumer price intervention?
o: Only State Food Commissions and Fair Price Shops
Only private supermarkets licensed by NITI Aayog
NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar outlets and mobile vans
FCI warehouses and commercial banks בלבד
accepted.x: Bharat-brand atta, rice and dal are sold at subsidised retail prices through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar outlets, as well as mobile vans.
accepted.tq: Match the intervention with its complete distribution-channel combination.
accepted.sec: Price interventions - Bharat Rice, Bharat Atta via NAFED, NCCF, Kendriya Bhandar  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The National Cooperative Consumers’ Federation of India (NCCF) was set up in:
accepted.x: NCCF was established in 1965.
accepted.tq: Recall the establishment year using close decade-based distractors.
accepted.sec: Price interventions - Bharat Rice, Bharat Atta via NAFED, NCCF, Kendriya Bhandar  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: NCCF functions under which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Finance
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Rural Development
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
accepted.x: NCCF functions under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.
accepted.tq: Use the ministry-association trap by distinguishing neighbouring economic ministries.
accepted.sec: Price interventions - Bharat Rice, Bharat Atta via NAFED, NCCF, Kendriya Bhandar  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the functions of NCCF?
o: It fixes constitutional food entitlements and hears NFSA appeals.
It procures essential goods and conducts price-stabilisation operations.
It exclusively manages strategic reserves of wheat and rice.
It regulates stock exchanges and issues currency notes.
accepted.x: NCCF procures essential goods and undertakes price-stabilisation operations. It is not the constitutional authority for food entitlements, the exclusive manager of strategic reserves, or a financial regulator.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct body-function pair and reject authority swaps.
accepted.sec: Price interventions - Bharat Rice, Bharat Atta via NAFED, NCCF, Kendriya Bhandar  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the proposed Draft NFS (Amendment) Bill, 2026?
o: It proposes 7 kg per person for AAY, subject to a cap of 35 kg.
It abolishes the AAY entitlement and provides only wheat.
It proposes 35 kg per person for every AAY household without any cap.
It fixes the AAY entitlement at 5 kg per unit without a household ceiling.
accepted.x: The draft proposal provides 7 kg per person for AAY, with the total entitlement capped at 35 kg.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a per-person proposal from the overall household cap.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following is identified as a proposed reform programme for the period 2026–31?
o: AAY-FCI-1997
OMSS-2013
SARTHAK-PDS
TPDS-2005
accepted.x: SARTHAK-PDS 2026–31 is identified as a proposed reform programme in the food distribution sector.
accepted.tq: Match the named programme with its stated period.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following is a stated criticism of the present food subsidy framework?
o: Issue prices have remained frozen since 2013 while subsidy costs have risen.
The NFSA excludes all rural households from food support.
The PDS supplies only imported foodgrains and no domestic cereals.
Issue prices have increased every year while subsidies have been abolished.
accepted.x: A criticism is that issue prices have been frozen since 2013 even as the subsidy burden has increased.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise trend and avoid reversed or extreme statements.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which combination reflects the suggested expansion of the food-security basket and related convergence in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Imported wheat alone, with convergence with commercial banks
Sugar and petroleum, with convergence with the GST Council
Pulses, oil and fortified foods, with convergence with Anganwadi and MDM
Only cereals, with convergence limited to stock exchanges
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh is exploring a wider PDS basket including pulses, oil and fortified foods, along with convergence with Anganwadi and the Mid-Day Meal programme.
accepted.tq: Apply the policy proposal to the correct commodities and linked programmes.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which statement best captures the contemporary understanding of food security in the context of climate risk?
o: It concerns only urban households unable to purchase food.
It includes an affordable and nutritious food supply for about 1.4 billion people, not merely sufficient grain.
It concerns only producing enough cereals and excludes nutrition.
It is limited to maintaining strategic wheat reserves for emergencies.
accepted.x: Climate-related food-security concerns now include an affordable, nutritious supply for about 1.4 billion people, rather than only the availability of sufficient grain.
accepted.tq: Choose the comprehensive interpretation instead of the narrow cereal-only definition.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes poverty, hunger and unaffordability of a healthy diet?
o: They are unrelated and cannot occur together.
Only hunger has any connection with food affordability.
They are identical concepts and always affect exactly the same households.
They overlap but are not identical concepts.
accepted.x: Poverty, hunger and unaffordability of a healthy diet overlap in many cases, but they are not identical concepts.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between related concepts without treating them as synonyms.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations represents the major concerns raised about diversification of food support under the PDS?
o: Removing nutrition objectives and focusing only on storage
Replacing all cereals with imported pulses
Restricting food support to urban consumers
Adding eggs, milk and dietary diversity without reducing cereal support
accepted.x: The debate supports adding eggs, milk and dietary diversity while retaining cereal support rather than cutting it.
accepted.tq: Select the balanced policy position rather than an extreme replacement strategy.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
